title: LSAT PrepTest 101 Explanations: Every Logical Reasoning and Reading Comprehension Answer i
description: The answer key tells you what. It never tells you why. I've been coaching the LSAT since 2005, and the review habit that separates students who plateau from students who jump 10 to 30+ points is the same every time: they don't just check their answers, they argue with them. This book gives you the other side of that argument for every scored Logical Reasoning and Reading Comprehension question in LawHub PrepTest 101. Every explanation is original to LSAT Unplugged and built for the Socratic Review Method. You get the argument's structure, the gap the question lives in, why the right answer is right, why each trap is wrong, and the takeaway worth drilling. The book ends with a question-type index so you can drill Flaw, Necessary Assumption, Strengthen, Weaken, or any other pattern across the whole test. The book opens with two primers: a Logical Reasoning primer built on the question-type frequencies from all 59 current PrepTests, and a Reading Comprehension primer on reading for structure instead of detail. Logical Reasoning is 2/3 of your score. The primers make sure you're reviewing the right things before you review anything. One thing to know before you buy: no LSAT question text appears in this book. LSAC owns the questions, so these explanations reference them by question number, and you work with the official test open beside it through LawHub. That's how the book stays honest, and it's also how review actually works: real questions, then real explanations. Written for the current LSAT: 2 scored Logical Reasoning sections and 1 scored Reading Comprehension section, no Logic Games. Want all 59 PrepTests?
